operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2 of Executive Order 10897 (25 FR 12429) states that Executive Order No. 9941 "is hereby superseded." Section 3 states that the order "shall be effective as" of "October 16,1960", and that the Secretary of State may make rules issued under section 1 "effective on or after that date." The first end is therefore recorded as 1960-10-16, the effective date the superseding order states for itself; the order was signed December 2, 1960 and published December 6, 1960, so the alternative reading dates the supersession 1960-12-02. The actor is the President (Dwight D. Eisenhower) and the mechanism is express supersession of the entire order, which had a single operative paragraph. The delegation is replaced by section 1(a) and (c) of the superseding order, so the clause has no continuing predicate on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 9941 (March 26, 1948; 13 FR 1625) is a single paragraph that authorizes the Secretary of State to exercise the President's authority under sections 801(a) and 881(a) of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 to prescribe rules for the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System and for deposits of voluntary contributions into the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability Fund. Section 2 of Executive Order 10897 (signed December 2, 1960; 25 FR 12429, from the Federal Register text held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10897.txt) provides that Executive Order No. 9941 "is hereby superseded." Section 3 of that order provides that it "shall be effective as" of "October 16,1960". The order is therefore no longer in force on 2026-10-14. The status of this order was undecided, with no adopted provisional status. It is judged here from the order's own single command, the held text of the superseding order, the Office of the Federal Register disposition note ('Superseded by: EO 10897, December 2, 1960') and the bounded searches, all of which agree. The first end is recorded as the effective date stated in section 3 of Executive Order 10897 (1960-10-16), not its signing date (1960-12-02); a reader who treats the supersession as operative only from signing would date it 1960-12-02. Either date precedes the cutoff.

A search of the held order texts for the number 9941 found only Executive Order 10897 (its Federal Register text and an American Presidency Project copy), and Federal Register page texts for Executive Orders 9940 and 10898 that print this order or the superseding section on the same page; no earlier revocation or supersession exists. The Office of the Federal Register note on Executive Order 10897 records that it was later revoked by Executive Order 12292 (February 23, 1981), whose section 10(g) lists Executive Order No. 10897; the held text of Executive Order 12292 does not name Executive Order 9941 and contains no revival, and a revocation of the superseding order does not by itself restore a superseded one, so the supersession of Executive Order 9941 stands.","independent_command_check":"The paragraph contains one command, a delegation of two statutory presidential authorities (sections 801(a) and 881(a) of the Foreign Service Act of 1946) for one purpose, internal management of the Government. The section 3 effective date applies to Executive Order 10897 as a whole, including its section 2."}

savings_residuals.reason: The authority that Executive Order 9941 delegated is re-delegated to the Secretary of State by section 1(a) and (c) of Executive Order 10897 (sections 801(a) and 881(a) of the Foreign Service Act of 1946), and section 3 of that order lets the Secretary make rules issued under section 1 effective on or after October 16, 1960. Executive Order 9941 created no right, fund or pending proceeding of its own, so nothing survives under this order independently of its successor.
